﴿with their Lord﴾; i.e., under His guarantee, or as a store kept for them with Him, the reality of which none knows but Him, exalted is He.

﴿and He is their Protector﴾; i.e., their Master and their Helper.

﴿for what they used to do﴾: by reason of their righteous deeds, or He is their Guardian in recompensing them for them, by taking charge of delivering it to them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 128:

﴿And on the Day He gathers them all together﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb, either as an object (maf'ul bihi) or as a time adverb (zarf). It is also read with the first-person plural nun of majesty (nun al-'azamah), by way of iltifat (shift of grammatical person), to magnify the matter. The pronoun in the accusative refers to those who are gathered from the two species (al-thaqalan), that is: "And mention the Day He gathers the two species, saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾"; or "and the Day He gathers them, He says: O assembly of jinn"; or "and the Day He gathers them and says: O assembly of jinn," there being in that day of states and terrors what is too dreadful for words to express. The ma'shar (assembly) is the group, and by "the assembly of jinn" is meant the devils (shayatin).

﴿You have indeed taken many of mankind﴾; that is, you have taken many of them into seduction and misguidance, or you have taken them by making them your followers, so that they were gathered together with you, like the saying: "The commander has taken many of the soldiers (istakthara al-amir min al-junud)." This is by way of rebuke and reproach.

﴿And their allies among mankind will say﴾; that is, those who obeyed them.

The "min" in His words ﴿among mankind﴾ is either explanatory of the genus (li-bayan al-jins), meaning: their allies who are mankind; or it is connected to an implied element that serves as a circumstantial clause (hal) of "their allies," meaning: being from mankind.

﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾; that is, mankind benefited from the jinn by their pointing them toward desires and what leads to them. It is said: by their casting to them false reports, sorcery, and soothsaying; and the jinn enjoyed mankind by their obeying them and attaining their aims by the acceptance of what was cast to them. It is also said: the enjoyment of mankind by the jinn was that they used to seek refuge with them in deserts (mafawiz) and places of fear, and the enjoyment of the jinn by mankind was their acknowledgment that the jinn were able to grant them protection.

﴿And we have reached our appointed term which You appointed for us﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. They said this as an acknowledgment of what they had done of obeying the devils, following desire, and denying the resurrection, and as a manifestation of regret over it, and grief over their state, and submission to their Lord. Perhaps the restriction to reporting the speech of the misguided is to indicate that the misleaders have been utterly silenced, so that they were unable to speak at all.

﴿He says﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) built upon a question arising from the report of their speech, as if it were said: "What then did God Most High say at that time?" So it was said: "He says."

﴿The Fire is your abode﴾; that is, your dwelling-place, or the state of your sojourning, just as the Abode of Peace is the abode of the believers.

﴿Abiding therein﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), and its governing element is "your abode" if it is taken as a verbal noun (masdar); and the meaning of the annexation applies if it is taken as a place.

﴿Except as God wills﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: God Most High excepted a people whom He knew beforehand would become Muslims and would affirm the Prophet (ﷺ). This is based on the view that the exception is not part of what is reported, and that "ma" means "man" (those who).

It is also said: the meaning is: except the times in which they are transferred from the Fire to the zamharir (extreme cold), for it is related that they enter a valley in which there is such cold that it separates some of their joints from others, so they cry out and ask to be returned to the blazing Hell.

It is also said: a gate to Paradise will be opened for them while they are in the Fire, so they hasten toward it, but when they reach it, the gate is shut upon them. In both interpretations the exception is one of mockery toward them. It is also said: "except what God wills" refers to the time before entering, as if it were said: "The Fire is your abode forever, except for the period He grants you respite," but its remoteness is not hidden.

﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise﴾ in His acts.

﴿All-Knowing﴾ of the states of the two species and their deeds, and of the recompense befitting them.

{And thus} i.e., in the same manner as was set forth regarding the empowerment of the jinn to lead humans astray and mislead them.

﴿We shall make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾ from among humankind,

﴿of others﴾ — another group among them; i.e., We shall place them in such a state that they become allies to one another through misguidance and leading astray, or We shall make some of them companions of others in punishment, just as they were so in the world when they committed the ugly deeds that lead to it.

﴿because of what they used to earn﴾ — because of their being persistent in their earning, namely disbelief and sins.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 130:

﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind﴾ This begins the relating of what will come of the rebuke and reproach of the two assemblies for their neglect of what concerns their own selves, following the relating of the rebuke of the assembly of jinn for misleading and leading astray humankind, and the explanation of the outcome of their affair.

﴿Did there not come to you﴾; that is, in the worldly life.

﴿Messengers﴾; that is, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But not in the sense that every messenger came to every one of the nations; rather, that a messenger specific to each nation came to it. That is: Did there not come to every nation of you a particular messenger?

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿from among you﴾ is connected to an omitted element that functions as an attributive modifier of "messengers"; that is, existing from among your company. But not in the sense that they are of the kind of both groups together; rather, they are from humankind alone. They were described as being from both only either to emphasize the obligation to follow them and to signal the closeness of the two in essence and their unity in obligation and address, as if they were a single kind; and for this reason one of them was able to lead the other astray. Or because the intended meaning of "messengers" is that which includes the messengers of the messengers, and it is established that the jinn listened to the Qur'an and warned their people with it, as is expressed by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We turned toward you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an﴾ up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿who relate to you My verses﴾ is another attributive modifier of "messengers," confirming what is meant by the sending of messengers, namely conveying and warning; and this has been accomplished with respect to both communities (the two weighty ones).

﴿and warn you﴾ with what is among its contents of terrifying matters.

﴿of the meeting of this your day﴾, the Day of Gathering, in which they have witnessed what has been prepared for them of the various kinds of tremendous punishments.

﴿They will say﴾ This is a resumptive statement based on a question arising from the preceding speech, as if it were said: What did they say at that severe rebuke? So it is said: They said.

﴿We testify against ourselves﴾; that is, to the coming of the messengers and their warning, and to their confronting them with disbelief and denial, and to their deserving, because of that, the everlasting punishment, as detailed in the relating of their answer to the question of the guardians of the Fire, where they said: ﴿Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied and said, "Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error."﴾ Here it has been stated concisely in the relating, just as their answer was stated concisely, where they said: ﴿Yes, but the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the worldly life deceived them﴾, together with what is joined to it, is a parenthetical clause explaining what led them in the world to commit the abominations they committed, and what compelled them in the Hereafter, after that, to confess to disbelief and to deserving punishment, and a censure of them for that; that is: They were deceived in the world by the lowly life, and by the vile, perishing pleasures, and turned away from the enduring bliss of which the messengers gave good news, and dared to commit what would draw them to the everlasting punishment of which they had been warned.

﴿And they will testify﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿against themselves that they were﴾ in the world.

﴿disbelievers﴾; that is, in the signs and warnings brought by the messengers in the detail mentioned just above; and they were compelled to submit to the most severe punishment, as is indicated by what is related of them in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾ In this there is an exposure of their loss and a warning to the hearers against the likes of their conduct that is beyond any further addition.

**Abu al-Su'ud, Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim, on surah 6, verse 131:**

﴿That﴾ refers to what was mentioned of their testifying against themselves to their disbelief and to their deserving punishment. The address is to the Messenger ﷺ by way of *talwin* (shifting the mode of address). It is the *mubtada'* (subject), and its *khabar* (predicate) is the words of the Exalted: ﴿that your Lord would not destroy the cities﴾, with the *lam* elided, on the basis that *an* is *masdariyyah* (forming a verbal noun), or that it is *mukhaffafah* (the light form) of *inna*, and the pronoun of the matter (*damir al-sha'n*), which is its subject, is omitted.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿unjustly﴾ are connected either to *muhlik* (destroying), meaning "because of an injustice," or to an omitted element that stands as a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier) of "the cities," meaning "while they are characterized by injustice." The people's being characterized by injustice is a characterization of the city through them.

As for it being a *hal* of "your Lord," or of the pronoun in "*muhlik*," as has been said, this is refuted by the fact that the heedlessness of its people is necessarily included in the meaning and reality of injustice. Therefore it is not fitting to restrict it by the words of the Exalted: ﴿while its people are heedless﴾. The meaning is: that is established because it is not the case that your Lord would destroy the cities *because of* a cause, that is, any injustice they committed, from among the instances of injustice, before they were forbidden from it and alerted to its falsehood through a Messenger and a Book, even though the immediate judgment of reason decides it, and before they were warned of the consequence of their crimes. In other words, were it not for the absence of Him, the Exalted, punishing them before the sending of the messengers and the revelation of the books, it would not have been possible to rebuke them for what was mentioned, nor would they have testified against themselves to their disbelief and their deserving of punishment, nor would they have offered the excuse of the non-arrival of messengers, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾

What has been mentioned was given as the reason for the absence of worldly punishment, which is the destruction of the cities before warning, although the closer reasoning for the absence of punishment of any kind without the sending of messengers is more complete, as expressed in the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We would not punish until We had sent a messenger﴾. This is to demonstrate the perfection of His, glorified and exalted is He, transcendence above both kinds of punishment, worldly and otherworldly together, without warning, in the most eloquent and emphatic manner, since the statement is restricted to negating worldly punishment from Him, the Exalted, so that the negation of otherworldly punishment from Him, the Exalted, is established by way of demonstrative proof through the principle of greater priority.

For since He, the Exalted, did not punish them with a light, temporary punishment without warning, then He would surely not punish them with a severe, everlasting punishment, which is more fitting and more evident. Had it been given as the reason the negation of punishment as mentioned, it would have been understood, according to the context, as referring to what the discourse is about, namely the negation of otherworldly punishment, while the negation of worldly punishment would not be addressed either explicitly or by implication, because the negation of the higher does not indicate the negation of the lower. Moreover, the consequence of worldly punishment upon warning, when those warned are not affected by it, is known and observed by the listeners, so they infer from that that otherworldly punishment is likewise, and so they refrain from neglecting the duties of warning with the utmost restraint. This is what the eloquence of the noble arrangement of the Qur'an requires.

As for making ﴿that﴾ a reference to the sending of the messengers, peace be upon them, and their warning, with the predicate of the subject omitted as the majority have agreed, this is far removed from the requirement of the context. And God, glorified is He, knows best.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 132:

﴿And for each there are degrees﴾; that is, among the accountable beings of both the two weighty creations (humans and jinn).

﴿Degrees﴾: varying ranks and differing tiers.

﴿According to what they did﴾: according to their deeds, whether good or evil. For their deeds are degrees in themselves; or [the degrees are] according to the recompense for their deeds, since every recompense is a specific rank assigned to them; or [the meaning is] on account of their deeds.

﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾: so that no deed of theirs, nor the measure of reward or punishment they deserve for it, is hidden from Him. It is also read with the (second person) ta' (taqūnūn / ta'malūn), by way of giving precedence to address (khitab) over the third person (ghayba).

Your Lord is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), full of Mercy (dhu al-rahma). This is a subject and predicate; that is, He is known as the One who is independent (ghani) of everything other than Himself, whoever or whatever that may be, so His independence from the servants and from their worship is included in it. The mention of the attribute of lordship (rububiyya) in both places, especially in the second, because it is the place of the pronoun with an added pronoun referring to him ﷺ, shows kindness toward him (ﷺ) and clears his sacred presence from any suspicion that the threat coming afterward also includes him, which is clear.

And His saying, exalted is He: "dhu al-rahma" (full of Mercy) is another predicate, or it is the predicate, and "al-Ghani" is a descriptive attribute. That is, He shows mercy to them by imposing obligations upon them for their perfection, and He grants them respite in their disobedience. In this there is an alert that what was mentioned earlier about sending (the messengers) was not for His benefit, but out of His mercy toward the servants, and a preparation for His saying, exalted is He: "in yashа yudhhibkum" (if He wills, He will take you away). That is: He has no need of you; if He wills, He will take you away, O disobedient ones. In the shift of address there is an intensification of the threat, which is clear.

"wa yastakhlif min ba'dikum" (and He will make succeed after you): that is, after your removal.

"ma yasha'u" (whom He wills) of creation. The use of "ma" rather than "man" is to show the perfection of majesty and to remove them from the rank of rational beings.

"kama ansha'akum min dhurriyyati qawmin akharin" (as He produced you from the offspring of another people): that is, from the descendants of other peoples who were not of your kind, namely the people of Noah's ship, peace be upon him, but He kept you alive out of mercy toward you. The "ma" in "kama" is verbal (masdariyya), and the place of the kaf is in the accusative, as it is a comparative verbal noun not from the same root as the verb; since "yastakhlif" here carries the meaning of "yunshi'" (produce), it is as if it were said: "and He will produce a production like your production..." etc. Or it is an attribute of the verbal noun of the verb mentioned; that is, He will cause succession in a manner like your production... etc. And the conditional clause is a resumptive statement confirming what precedes it of independence and mercy.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 134:

﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ (p-188); that is, what you are promised of the Resurrection, and of the awesome matters that branch out from it. The form of the future tense here indicates continuous, renewing persistence.

﴿is coming (la-ātin)﴾: it will certainly befall, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely coming to pass﴾. Its being expressed by the active participle (ātin) rather than the verb is to show the perfection of the speed of its occurrence, by depicting it as a swift seeker that no fleeing person can escape. This is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you cannot escape﴾; that is, you cannot elude it, even if you ride in flight over the back of every difficult and easy (terrain). Likewise, the choice of the active participial form over the future tense is to announce the perfect nearness of its arrival.

The intended meaning is the statement of the continuance of the negation of inability (to escape), not the statement of the negation of the continuance of inability. For the nominal sentence, as it indicates the continuance of affirmation, when preceded by a negative particle, indicates by the help of context the continuance of negation, not the negation of continuance, as has been verified in its proper place.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 135:

﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your standing (makanatikum)"﴾. After their condition and their end had been explained to them in the form of direct address, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded, by way of shifting the mode of address (al-talwin), to confront them with intensified threat and repeated warning, and to display to them the utmost firmness in the religion, the utmost certainty in his matter, and indifference to them. That is: act to the full extent of your ability and capacity. It is said: "tamakkana makanatan" when one becomes firmly established to the utmost degree. Or it means: act according to your state and condition in which you are, from the expression "makan" and "makanah," like "maqam" and "maqamah." It has been read as "makanatikum" (in the plural). The meaning is: remain steadfast in your disbelief and your enmity.

﴿Indeed I am acting﴾ in accordance with what I have been commanded: steadfastness in Islam, continuing in righteous deeds, and perseverance. The expression of the threat in the form of an imperative is an intensification of the warning, as if the one threatening wishes to punish him with unanimous resolve, and so he compels him by the command to what leads to it. It also records that the one threatened can produce nothing from himself but evil, like what he has been commanded, such that he finds no way to escape from it.

﴿So you will come to know who will have the good outcome of the abode﴾. "Sawfa" is for emphasizing the content of the sentence, and the knowing (al-'ilm) is cognitive (irfani). "Man" is either an interrogative (istifhamiyyah) suspending the verb of knowing (mu'allaqah li-fi'l al-'ilm), its position being nominative by way of the inceptive (mahalluha al-raf' 'ala al-ibtida'). And "takunu" with its subject and predicate is a predicate for it, and it together with its predicate is in the accusative position by serving in place of the object of "ta'lamun"; that is: so you will come to know which of us will have the good outcome, the good end for which Allah the Exalted created these abodes.

Or it is a relative (mawsulah), its position being accusative as an object of "ta'lamun"; that is: so you will come to know the one for whom is the outcome of the abode. In it, together with the warning, there is fairness in speech and an alert to the perfect certainty of the warner in his matter. It has been read with the letter "ya" (ya'), because the feminine form of "'aqibah" is not real (ghayr haqiqi).

﴿Indeed, He﴾; that is: the matter (al-sha'n).

﴿The wrongdoers will not succeed﴾. The word "zulm" (wrongdoing) has been placed in the position of "kufr" (disbelief), as an indication that the impossibility of success follows from any single instance of wrongdoing, so what then of disbelief, which is the greatest of its instances.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 136:

﴿And they assign﴾ begins the condemnation of their appalling state, by relating their vile sayings and deeds. They were the polytheists of the Arabs, who designated certain portions of tilth (ḥarth) and livestock (nitāj) for God Most High, and other portions of them for their gods. When what they had designated for God Most High appeared to be pure and growing, increasing in goodness, they reverted and assigned it to their gods; and when what they had designated for their gods grew pure, they left it, pleading that God Most High is self-sufficient. This was nothing but out of love for their gods and their preference for them.

The verb jaʿl (assigning, making) is either transitive to one object, in which case the two prepositional phrases in His words ﴿for God, of what He has created﴾ (li-llāhi mimmā dhara'a) are attached to it.

The "min" in His words ﴿of the tilth and the livestock﴾ (min al-ḥarth wal-anʿām) is explanatory (bayān) of "mā" (what), and it contains an indication of the extent of their ignorance, in that they associated with the Creator, in His creation, an inanimate thing that has no power over anything, and then they preferred it over Him by assigning the pure portion to it; that is, they designated for God Most High, from what He had created, of the tilth and the livestock.

﴿A portion﴾ (naṣīban) which they devote to guests and the poor. Its being placed after the two prepositional phrases is due to the consideration, repeated many times, of giving importance to what is placed first and creating anticipation for what comes later.

Or the verb is transitive to two objects, the first of which is: "﴿of what He has created﴾" (mimmā dhara'a), with "min" being partitive; that is, they made some of what He had created a portion for Him. What has been said, that the first object is "portion" and the second is "for God," is not supported by the soundness of the meaning. And the narration of their assigning a portion to Him Most High indicates that they also assigned a portion to their associates.

"Portion" is not mentioned, being sufficed by His words ﴿So they say: This is for God, by their claim, and this is for our associates﴾. It was also read with a damma on the zāy (zakī), which is a dialectal variant of it. The first was restricted by it only to alert that, in reality, it is not an act of worship for God Most High that entails no reward whatsoever, like voluntary acts by which the Face of God Most High is sought. It is not, as has been said, for alerting that this is something they invented which God Most High did not command them to do, for that is derived from the act of assigning, and for this reason the second was not restricted by it.

It is possible that this is a preparation for what follows, in the sense that their saying "this is for God" is a mere claim on their part, and they do not act in accordance with its requirement, which is its being exclusively for Him Most High.

So His words ﴿Then what was for their associates does not reach God, and what was for God reaches their associates﴾ are an explanation and elaboration of it; that is: what they designated for their associates is not directed to the purposes to which what they designated for God Most High is directed, namely the hospitality of guests and almsgiving to the poor. And what they designated for God Most High, when they found it pure, is directed to the purposes to which what they designated for their gods is directed, namely expenditure upon them, slaughtering their sacrifices at them, paying the stipends of their custodians, and the like.

﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ regarding what they did, of preferring their gods over God Most High, and acting upon what was not prescribed for them. Here "mā" carries the meaning of "alladhī" (what), and the estimated sense is: "Evil is that which their judgment judges," so "their judgment" is the subject (mubtada'), and what precedes it is the predicate (khabar), and it has been elided due to the indication of "﴿they judge﴾" upon it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 137:

﴿And thus﴾ Like that adornment, namely the adorning of shirk (polytheism) in the division of offerings between God Most High and their deities; or, like that eloquent adornment that is known from the satans.

﴿Their partners adorned for many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ by burying them alive and slaughtering them for their gods. In the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) a man would swear: "If God grants me such-and-such a number of boys, I will surely slaughter one of them," just as ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib swore, and this is well known.

﴿Their partners﴾: that is, their allies among the jinn, or among the custodians (sadana) of the idols. It is the subject of "adorned" (zayyana), placed after the adverbial phrase and the object for reasons that have been mentioned more than once.

It is also read with the verb in the passive, with the killing as its subject, the children in the accusative, and the partners in the genitive, by attributing the killing to them, with the separation between them by its object.

It is also read with the verb in the passive, with "killing" in the nominative and "their children" in the genitive, and "their partners" in the nominative, by supposing a verb implied by "adorned," as if it were said: "The killing of their children was adorned for them," and then it was asked: "Who adorned it?" and the answer was: "Their partners adorned it."

﴿So that they might destroy them﴾: that is, that they might ruin them through misguidance.

﴿And that they might confuse for them their religion﴾: and that they might mix up for them what they were upon of the religion of Isma'il, peace be upon him, or what it was obligatory for them to adhere to in religion. The "lam" (la) is of purpose if the adornment is from the satans, and of consequence if it is from the custodians.

﴿And had God willed﴾: that is, that they not do that.

﴿They would not have done it﴾: that is, the polytheists would not have done the killing with which they were adorned, or the partners would not have adorned it, or the destruction and confusion; or both parties, all of that, with the pronoun treated as a demonstrative.

﴿So leave them and what they fabricate﴾: the "fa" is explanatory (fasiha); that is, since what they did was by the will of God Most High, leave them and their fabrication, or "and what they fabricate" of falsehood, for in what God Most High wills there are profound wisdoms. ﴿Indeed, We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾. In this there is of severity of warning what is not hidden.

[Abu al-Su'ud, *Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim*, on Surah 6, verse 138]

﴿And they say﴾: this narrates another kind of their disbelief.

﴿This﴾ is a pointer to what they designated for their idols. The feminine form is for the predicate (khabar, the predicate of a nominal sentence).

﴿Cattle and tilth, ḥijr﴾: that is, forbidden (ḥarām). Ḥijr is a verbal noun (fi'l) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ūl), like dhibḥ (slaughter), which is the same for the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, because its origin is the verbal noun (maṣdar). For this reason it functions as a qualifier (ṣifah) of "cattle and tilth."

It is also read as ḥujr with a damma, with two dammas, and as ḥirj, meaning narrow (ḍayyiq). Its original form is ḥarij. It is said that it is a transposed form (maqlūb) of ḥijr.

﴿None may eat of it except whom we will﴾: they mean that only men, not women, may serve the idols. This sentence is another qualifier of "cattle and tilth."

﴿By their claim﴾ is attached to an omitted element which is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of the agent of "they say." That is: they said it while attached to their false claim, without any proof.

﴿And cattle﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, and the sentence is conjoined (ma'ṭūf) to His words, ﴿This is cattle…﴾ and so on. That is: they said, pointing to another portion of their cattle: "And these are cattle."

﴿Their backs are forbidden﴾: by these they mean the baḥā'ir (slit-eared she-camels), the sawā'ib (freed animals), and the ḥawāmī (protected animals).

﴿And cattle﴾: that is, "And these are cattle," as already mentioned.

As for His words, ﴿They do not mention the name of God over them﴾, this is a qualifier of "cattle," but it does not occur in their quoted speech, like its counterparts; rather it is brought from His side, to specify the qualified thing and distinguish it from others, as in His words: ﴿and their saying, "We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of God"﴾, according to one of the interpretations. It is as if it were said: "And cattle that were slaughtered for the idols," for they are the ones over which the name of God is not mentioned, and over which only the names of the idols are mentioned.

It is also said: they do not perform the pilgrimage (ḥajj) on them, for the pilgrimage is not devoid of the mention of God the Exalted. Mujahid said: among their cattle there was a group which they did not mention God's name over, nor in anything concerning them: neither when they rode them, nor when they milked them, nor when they gave birth, nor when they sold them, nor when they carried loads on them.

﴿Inventing a lie against Him﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar). It is either because what they said is a fabrication (taqawwul) against God the Exalted, or because of an implied verb from the same root, meaning: "they fabricated a fabrication." The prepositional phrase is attached either to "they said," or to the implied "they fabricated," or to an omitted element which is a qualifier of it, not to "fabrication," because an emphatic verbal noun (maṣdar mu'akkid) does not govern. Or it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state of the agent of "they said," meaning: "fabricating." Or it is in the accusative as a cause, meaning: "for the sake of fabricating," so the prepositional phrase is attached to it.

﴿He will requite them for what they used to fabricate﴾: that is, on account of it or in exchange for it. The vagueness of the requital contains a dread that is not hidden.

﴿وَقالُوا﴾ ("And they say") is a report of another category of their disbelief.

﴿ما في بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأنْعامِ﴾ ("What is in the bellies of these cattle") they mean by it the fetuses of the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ears were slit and released, considered sacred) and the *sa'iba* (an animal set free for idols).

﴿خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا﴾ ("is exclusively for our males") is lawful for them alone. The *ta'* (ة) in *khalisa* is for transferring the word into the category of a noun (*ism*), or for intensification (*mubalagha*), or because *khalisa* is a verbal noun (*masdar*), like *'afiya*, placed in the position of the adjective *khalis* for emphasis, or because an opposite has been omitted, meaning "possessor of exclusivity," or for feminine agreement, based on taking *ma* to refer to the fetuses.

The masculine form in His saying, ﴿وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أزْواجِنا﴾ ("and forbidden to our wives"), means "the category of our wives," and they are females grammatically. In this, as you see, the noble text is read against the usual practice, which is to agree first with the wording and then with the meaning, as in His saying, ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَسْتَمِعُ إلَيْكَ وجَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ ...﴾ ("And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed veils over their hearts...") and its like.

As for the reverse, they said there is no parallel to it in the Qur'an. This ruling from them applies if that is born alive, which is the apparent and customary case.

﴿وَإنْ يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً﴾ ("But if it is dead") means: if it is born dead.

﴿فَهُمْ﴾ ("then they") means: the males and females.

﴿فِيهِ﴾ ("in it") means: in what is in the bellies of the cattle. It was also said that the intended sense of *maytah* (dead) covers both male and female, so the masculine was given precedence over the feminine.

﴿شُرَكاءُ﴾ ("are partners"): they all eat from it together. It was read *khalisatan* (in the accusative), as an emphatic verbal noun (*masdar mu'akkid*), with the predicate being *li-dhukurina*; or as a circumstantial state (*hal*) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase (*zarf*), not from the pronoun in *dhukurina*, nor from *al-dhukur*, because it may not precede the implicit governing agent (*'amil ma'nawi*), nor its genitive-marked referent. It was also read *khalisuh* (in the nominative with a pronominal suffix), as a substitute (*badal*) for *ma*, or as a second subject (*mubtada' thani*).

﴿سَيَجْزِيهِمْ وصْفَهُمْ﴾ ("He will repay them for their description") means: the recompense for their describing falsehood against God, the Exalted, concerning permitting and forbidding, from His saying, ﴿وَتَصِفُ ألْسِنَتُهُمُ الكَذِبَ﴾ ("and their tongues describe falsehood").

﴿إنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ("Indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing") is a justification for the threat of recompense, for the All-Wise, All-Knowing who knows what proceeded from them would hardly leave their recompense, which is among the requirements of wisdom.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 140:

﴿Indeed, they have lost who killed their children﴾ is the answer to an omitted oath. It is also read with the intensive form (qatt'ala, tashdid). They are Rabi'a, Mudar, and their likes among the Arabs, who used to bury their daughters alive, out of fear of captivity (sabi) and poverty; that is, they lost their religion and their worldly life.

﴿in folly, without knowledge﴾ is connected to "killed" as its cause (ʿilla): that is, because of the lightness of their minds and their ignorance that Allah is the Provider for them and for their children. Or it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal); what supports this is that it is read as "sufaha'" (foolish ones). Or it is an infinitive (masdar).

﴿and forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾ refers to the baha'ir, the sawa'ib, and the like.

﴿fabricating against Allah﴾ is in the accusative according to one of the aforementioned possibilities. The explicit mention of the Name of Majesty in place of the pronoun serves to show the full extent of their defiance and transgression.

﴿They have indeed gone astray﴾ from the straight path.

﴿and they were not guided﴾ to it, even if they were guided by various kinds of guidance; or it means they were never guided from the outset because of the corruption of their conduct. In that case the clause is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD), and according to the first reading it is coordinated (ʿatf) with "have gone astray."

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 141:**

﴿It is He who produced gardens, both trellised and untrellised﴾. This is a preface to what follows of the detailed account of the livestock (al-an'am). That is, He is the one who produced them without any partner in that in any way. The trellised (al-ma'rushat) among the vines are those raised upon what supports them.

﴿and untrellised﴾. These are the ones spread upon the surface of the earth. It has also been said: the trellised are those planted and trellised by people, and the untrellised are those that grow in the deserts and mountains.

﴿and the palm trees and the crops﴾ is coordinated with "gardens"; that is, He produced them both.

﴿varying in their produce﴾. It is also read as "ukluhu" (أُكْلُهُ) with the kaf vowelless; that is, its fruit that is eaten, in its form and manner. The pronoun may refer either to the palm trees, with the crops included in its ruling, or to the crops, with the rest analogous to it, or to all of them, on the assumption of "ukul dhalika," or to each of the two. "Varying" (mukhtalifan) is a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah), since it was not so at the time of production.

﴿and the olives and pomegranates﴾; that is, He produced both of them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause; that is, some of their individual members resemble one another in color, form, or taste, and some do not resemble one another.

﴿Eat of their fruit﴾; that is, of the fruit of each one of these.

﴿when it bears fruit﴾, even if it has not ripened and has not yet become fully ripe. It has also been said: its purpose is to permit the owner to eat from it before the payment of God's right.

﴿and give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. What is meant by this is what used to be given in charity on the day of harvest as an obligation, without specifying the amount, not the prescribed zakat, since zakat was made obligatory in Madinah and the surah is Makki (revealed in Makkah).

It has also been said that it refers to zakat, and that the verse is Madani (revealed in Madinah). The command to give it on the day of harvest is so that it is attended to at that time and is not delayed beyond the time of payment, and so that it is known that the obligation arises at the time of gathering, not at the time of winnowing. It is also read as "yawma hisadihi" (يَوْمَ حِصادِهِ) with a kasra on the ha', and this is a dialectal variant of it.

﴿and do not be wasteful﴾; that is, in giving charity. As it is narrated from Thabit ibn Qays that he harvested five hundred palm trees, then distributed all of their fruit and did not bring any of it into his house, in accordance with His saying: ﴿and do not stretch it out completely outstretched...﴾ the verse.

﴿Indeed, He does not love the wasteful﴾; that is, He does not approve of their wastefulness.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 142:

﴿And of the cattle, some for carrying loads and some for lying low (for slaughter).﴾ This begins the detailed account of the state of the cattle, and the refutation of what they fabricated against Allah, the Exalted, concerning them by way of prohibition and permission. It is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the object of "anshaʾa" (He produced), and "min" (of) is connected to it. That is: and He produced from the cattle that which is used for carrying burdens and that which is spread out for slaughter, or that which is spread out, made from their hair, wool and fur. It has been said: the large ones suitable for carrying, and the small ones close to the ground, as if they were a spread-out carpet upon which things are laid.

﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you.﴾ "Ma" (what) refers to what was mentioned of the carrying animals and the spread ones, and "min" (of) is partitive (tabʿiḍiyya); that is: eat some of what Allah, the Exalted, has provided for you, that is, His lawful provision. In this there is an explicit statement that their creation was for their benefit and welfare.

﴿And do not follow﴾ in the matter of permitting and forbidding, by imitating your ancestors who rashly engaged in that on their own initiative, fabricating against Allah, glorified is He.

﴿the footsteps of Satan.﴾ For that from them was by his seduction and his leading them astray.

﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ Manifest in enmity.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 143:

﴿Eight pairs﴾. The "zawj" (pair): that which has with it another of its own kind with which it pairs, and from which offspring comes about. What is meant by it is the four types. Presenting them under this heading and this number is a preparation for what the discourse has been brought to, namely the denunciation concerning the prohibition of each of the male and the female, and of what is in their wombs. It is a substitute (badal) for "﴿carrying animals and [animals for] spreading [on the ground]﴾", governed in the accusative by what governed both of them. Making it an object of "﴿eat﴾" is possible, with the saying of the Exalted, "﴿And do not follow﴾ ... " the verse standing as an interjection (mu'taridh) between them.

Or it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from "mā" in the sense of "differing" or "many." This is rejected by the eloquence (jaza'lah) of the noble composition, since it is evident that it is brought to clarify the state of the livestock: first by dividing them into carrying animals and spreading animals, then by dividing them into eight pairs, which result from the division of the first into camels and cattle, and the division of the second into sheep and goats, and then the division of each of the four categories into male and female. All of this is to define the materials about which they had fabricated lies against Him, the Glorified and Exalted, through permitting and forbidding, and then to rebuke them by exposing their lying and fabrication in every one of those materials, by directing the denunciation to each of them in detail.

As for "﴿two﴾" in the saying of the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿of the sheep, two﴾, it is a substitute for "﴿eight pairs﴾", in the accusative by its governor, which is the operator in "min"; that is: He produced from the sheep two pairs: the ram and the ewe. (p-193)

It is also read as "ithnani" (two) on the basis of inception (ibtida'). "Ad-da'n" (sheep) is a collective noun like "al-ibil" (camels), and its plural is "da'in," like "amir," or the plural of "da'in," like "tajir" and "tajr." It is also read with a fatha on the hamza.

﴿And of the goats, two﴾ is conjoined to its like, sharing with it in its ruling; that is: and He produced from the goats two pairs: the he-goat and the she-goat. It is read with a fatha on the 'ayn, which is the plural of "ma'iz," like "sahib" and "sahb," and "haris" and "hars." It is also read: "wa-min al-mi'za."

These four pairs are a detail of the "spreading" animals. Perhaps their being mentioned first in the detail, though their origin is mentioned later in the summary, is because these two kinds are the ones subject to eating, which is the greater part of what relates to lawfulness and prohibition. This is the secret of restricting the command to it in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Eat of what Allah has provided you﴾, without mention of benefiting from carrying and riding, or other things they prohibited concerning the sa'ibah and its kin.

﴿Say﴾: a turning of the address and a directing of it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), following the detailing of the kinds of livestock which He produced; that is: Say, rebuking them and showing their inability to answer.

﴿The two males﴾ from those two kinds, which are the ram and the he-goat.

﴿Has forbidden﴾; that is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as you claim that He is the one who forbids.

﴿Or the two females﴾: they are the ewe and the she-goat. The accusative of "the two males" and "the two females" is by "harrama," and it is positioned after them in meaning, though it occurs between them in form.

Likewise the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain﴾; that is: or what the females of the two kinds have carried, has He forbidden it, whether male or female?

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Inform me with knowledge...﴾ etc., is a repetition of the demand and a reiteration of the rebuke and confounding; that is: Inform me of a matter known from Allah, the Exalted, from the Book or from the reports of the prophets, indicating that He, the Exalted, forbade something of what has been mentioned; or: Inform me with an informing mingled with knowledge issuing from Him.

﴿If you are truthful﴾; that is: in your claim that He has forbidden it, Glory be to Him.

And His saying, ﴿and of camels, two﴾, is coordinated with His saying, "two of the sheep" (from the sheep, two). That is, He produced two of the camels: the male camel and the she-camel.

﴿And of cattle, two﴾: a male and a female.

﴿Say﴾: to silence them concerning these two kinds as well.

﴿Are the two males﴾ of them forbidden,

﴿or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ of those two kinds. The meaning is a denial that God, glorified is He, forbade them any of the four kinds, and a demonstration of their lying in this matter. The detailing of the males, the females, and what is in their wombs is for the sake of emphasis in refuting them, by presenting the denial against every category of their fabrications. For they would sometimes forbid the males of the livestock, and at other times their offspring whatever their condition, attributing all of this to God, glorified is He.

The reason the detail of each of the two kinds of the young and the two kinds of the adult is followed by the matter mentioned, with the interrogative (istifham) and denial, while also producing rebuke, is that the matter is put after the detailing of the four kinds, by saying: "Say: Is it the males He forbade, or the females, or what the wombs of the females contain?" Repeating and doubling (the question) gives greater emphasis in rebuke and binding them to their claim.

His saying, ﴿Or were you witnesses﴾, is a repetition of the silencing, like His saying, "Inform me with knowledge." The "am" is disjunctive (munqati'ah), the meaning of the hamza is denial and reproach, and the meaning of "bal" (rather) is a shift from what was mentioned to rebuke by another way; that is, "Rather, you were present and observing."

﴿When God enjoined this upon you﴾: that is, at the time He enjoined you with this prohibition. For you do not believe in any prophet, so there is no way for you, according to what your doctrine leads to, to know such things except by observation and hearing. In this there is a belittling of their intellects and a mockery of them that is not hidden.

﴿Who is more wrong than one who fabricates a lie against God﴾, thereby attributing to Him the prohibition of what He did not prohibit? The intended ones are their elders and those who established this for them, or Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah, who was the founder of this evil, or all of them, since they share in the fabrication against Him, glorified and exalted is He. So which group is more wrong than a group who fabricated... etc.

The wrongdoing of all of them is not impaired by the fact that some of them invented it and some followed them. The fa' (so) is for ordering what follows upon the rebuke mentioned before and the demonstration of their lying and fabrication; that is, he is more wrong than every wrongdoer, though what is negated explicitly is superiority, not equality, as has passed more than once.

﴿To mislead people﴾ is connected to the fabrication.

﴿Without knowledge﴾ is connected to an omitted element which stands as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of "fabricated"; that is, he fabricated against Him, exalted is He, while ignorant of the prohibition having come from Him, exalted is He. They were described as lacking knowledge of this, even though they know that it did not come from Him, exalted is He, to indicate that in wrongdoing they exceed all limits and ends. For whoever fabricates against Him, exalted is He, without knowledge that it came from Him, while there is the possibility that it did come from Him, is, if he is more wrong than every wrongdoer, then what is your opinion of one who fabricates against Him, exalted is He, while knowing that it did not come from Him? It is also permissible that it be a circumstantial clause from the subject of "to mislead"; that is, while being entangled in lack of knowledge of that which leads them to it.

﴿Indeed God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, whoever they are, to what is in their interest, sooner or later. And if this is the state of those characterized by wrongdoing in general, then what is your opinion of one who is at the furthest extreme of it?

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 145:

﴿Say﴾: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded, after silencing the polytheists and rebuking them, and after making clear that what they invent about the matter of prohibition is pure fabrication with no basis whatsoever, to explain to them what God has forbidden to them.

In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾, there is an indication that the criterion of what is lawful and what is unlawful is revelation, and that he (ﷺ) had searched through all that was revealed to him and examined carefully the prohibited things, and found nothing other than what has been detailed. In this there is an exaggeration in clarifying that the prohibited things are confined to that. "Forbidden" (muharraman) is an attribute of an omitted noun; that is: I do not find, as I have looked through what has been revealed to me, any forbidden food among the foods that they have forbidden.

﴿Upon one who eats﴾; that is: any eater whatsoever, male or female, in response to their saying: "It is forbidden for our wives."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿who eats it﴾ is for the sake of emphasis.

﴿Unless it be﴾; that is: that food.

﴿carrion﴾. It was also read as "takūna" with a ta', because the predicate is feminine; and it was read as "maytatun" with a raising (damma), with "kāna" being complete (taamma).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾ here is conjoined to "an yakūna" together with what is in its scope; that is: except the existence of carrion, or blood poured forth; that is: spilled, like the bloods that are in the veins, not like the spleen and the liver.

﴿or the flesh of swine, for indeed it﴾; that is: the swine.

﴿is an abomination﴾; that is: its flesh is filthy, because it habitually eats impurities, or it is vile.

﴿or a transgression﴾ is conjoined to "the flesh of swine," and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause affirming its prohibition.

﴿over which the name of other than God has been invoked﴾ is a descriptive qualifier clarifying it; that is: it was slaughtered in the name of idols. That was called a transgression only because of its extreme wickedness. It is also permissible that "transgression" be an object of purpose for "uhilla," and it is conjoined to "yakūna," and the pronoun returns to what the pronoun in "yakūna" returns to.

﴿So whoever is compelled﴾; that is: (p-195) one who is afflicted by the necessity compelling him to eat carrion in any of the compelling circumstances.

﴿neither desiring﴾ in that, over another compelled person like himself.

﴿nor transgressing﴾ the measure of necessity.

﴿indeed your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, exceedingly forgiving and merciful, who will not hold him accountable for that. The restriction to the first condition is not to show that if the restriction were absent the prohibition under discussion would still be realized; rather, it is to warn against another forbidden act, namely taking the right of another compelled person. For whoever takes the flesh of carrion from the hand of another compelled person and eats it, its prohibition is not by virtue of its being carrion flesh, but by virtue of its being a right of the other compelled person.

As for the second condition, it serves to confirm that the prohibition under discussion is definitively removed; for exceeding the amount with which the throat is sustained is forbidden insofar as it is carrion flesh. In the mention of the two attributes of forgiveness and mercy there is an indication that the disobedience remains, but that He, exalted is He, forgives him and has mercy upon him.

The verse is decisive (muhkama), because it indicates that he (ﷺ) did not find, in what was revealed to him up to that point, anything other than these. Its being followed later by the revelation of a prohibition of something else does not contradict this. Therefore it is not valid to cite it as evidence for abrogating the Book by a solitary report (khabar al-wahid), nor for the permissibility of things other than these, except with recourse to continuity of the original ruling (istishab).

﴿And upon those who were Jews﴾ specifically, not upon others among the earlier and later peoples.

﴿We forbade every animal with claws﴾; that is, every animal that has a digit from among camels, predators, and birds. It was also said: every animal with a talon or a hoof, and the hoof was called a claw (ظفر, *ẓufr*) figuratively (*majāzan*).

The consequence of their wrongdoing was the generalization of the prohibition, since some animals with claws had been lawful for them. When they did wrong, the prohibition extended to all of them. This confirms what preceded concerning the restriction of the prohibited things, and it clarifies, by refuting what contradicts it, the slander of the Jews and their denial of this. They used to say: "We are not the first to whom it was forbidden. It was forbidden only to Noah, Abraham, and those after them, until the matter reached us."

﴿And from the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fats﴾, not their flesh, for their flesh remains permitted. The fats (*shuḥūm*) are the fat covering the intestines (*thurūb*) and the fat of the kidneys. The genitive construction (*iḍāfa*) is for added binding.

﴿Except what their backs carry﴾ is an exception from the fats, and it excludes the fat that clings to their backs from the ruling of prohibition.

﴿Or the entrails (*ḥawāyā*)﴾ is conjoined to "their backs"; that is, what the entrails carry. *Ḥawāyā* is the plural of *ḥāwiya* or *ḥāwiyā'*, like *qāṣi'ā'* and *qawāṣi'*, or of *ḥawiyya*, like *safīna* and *safā'in*.

﴿Or what is mixed with bone﴾ is conjoined to "what they carry". It is the fat of the tail (*shaḥm al-alya*), and its being mixed with the bone means its attachment to the coccyx (*ʿujb al-dhanab*). It was also said that it is every fat attached to bone, from the ribs and others.

﴿That﴾ refers to the recompense and the prohibition. According to the first view, it is in the accusative (*naṣb*) as an emphatic verbal noun (*maṣdar mu'akkid*) for what follows it. According to the second view, it is a second object (*maf'ūl thānin*); that is, "that prohibition."

﴿We recompensed them for their rebellion﴾, that is, because of their wrongdoing, which was their killing of the prophets without right, their consuming of usury though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of people's wealth falsely. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them﴾. Whenever they committed an act of disobedience, they were punished by the prohibition of something from what had been made lawful for them, yet they denied this and claimed that these things had always been forbidden to the nations.

He refuted this for them and affirmed it with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾; that is, in all Our reports, of which this report is one. His saying, exalted is He, has indeed silenced them: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel forbade himself before the Torah was sent down. Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾.

It is narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) said this to them, they were struck dumb, and they did not dare to bring out the Torah, and how could they, when in it all that they feared was made clear with the utmost clarity?

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 147:

﴿And if they deny you﴾. It has been said: the pronoun refers to the Jews, because they are closer in mention, and because the polytheists are mentioned afterward by the title of association (ishrak). It has also been said: it refers to the polytheists. The meaning according to the first view: if the Jews deny you regarding the ruling mentioned, and persist in what they were upon of claiming the antiquity of the prohibition, ﴿then say﴾ to them:

﴿Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy﴾, who does not take you to account for every sin you commit, and gives you respite for some of them.

﴿And His punishment is not averted﴾ entirely,

﴿from the guilty people﴾. So do not deny what has happened from Him, exalted is He, of forbidding some good things to you as punishment and severity.

According to the second view: if the polytheists deny you regarding what has been detailed of the rulings on what is lawful and unlawful, then say to them: your Lord is possessed of vast mercy; He does not hasten punishment upon you for your denial. So do not be deceived by that, for it is a respite, not neglect.

It has also been said: He is merciful to the obedient and possessed of severe punishment for the guilty, so His words ﴿And His punishment is not averted...﴾ etc. have been put in its place, because it includes an alert to the descent of punishment upon them, together with the indication that it will certainly overtake them, with no deterrent turning it away from them at all.

"Those who associated partners (with God) will say," — a report of another form of their disbelief. Its announcement before it occurred, and then its occurrence as it was announced, is as His words narrate when it occurred: "And those who associated partners said: 'If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything.'" This is explicit that it is from God.

"If God had willed, we would not have associated partners" — meaning: if He had willed otherwise, by a will of approval, we ourselves would not have committed association.

"Nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything" — they meant by this that what they did was true and pleasing to God Most High, not an excuse for committing these abominations by God's willing them from them, such that their blame for it would stand as evidence for the Mu'tazilah. Do you not see His words, "Thus did those before them deny"? That is: just as these people denied you in that He prohibited association and did not forbid what they had forbidden, their predecessors denied the Messengers. This is explicit in what we have said. "Our fathers" is conjoined to the pronoun by the separation of "lā" (nor).

"Until they tasted Our might" which We sent down upon them for their denial.

"Say: Have you any knowledge" — any known matter that validly serves as proof for what you claim.

"That you bring it forth for us" — that is, that you show it to us.

"You follow only conjecture" — that is, in this you follow only false conjecture, which does not avail anything of the truth.

"And you do only guess" — you lie against God, Mighty and Majestic. There is in this no indication of prohibiting the following of conjecture absolutely; rather, what opposes it is definitive.

Say: "Then to God belongs the conclusive proof." The fa' (ف) is the response to an omitted conditional clause; that is, "It has become clear that you have no proof, so to God belongs the conclusive proof," i.e., the clear evidence that has reached the utmost firmness and steadiness, or by which its holder has established the soundness of his claim. What is meant by it is the Book, the Messenger, and the clarification, and they are among the "proofs" (hujaj) in the sense of intending, as though it aims at establishing the ruling and seeks it.

﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ That is, to the guidance by granting success to it and compelling you toward it. "But" (p-197) He did not will the guidance of everyone; rather, He willed the guidance of some, who directed their resolve toward following the path of truth, and the misguidance of others, who directed their choice to the opposite, without any compulsion turning them or any inclination diverting them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 150:

﴿Say: "Bring forth your witnesses."﴾ That is, bring them here. It is an imperative verb-noun (ism fi'l) that does not inflect according to the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, while in the dialect of Banu Tamim it is a verb that takes feminine and plural forms, according to the opinion of the majority (al-jumhur). Some have disagreed with them regarding its verbal status, but this is not valid. According to the Basrans, its original form is hálumma, from lamma (meaning: to intend), the alif being dropped to indicate the sukun on the lam, since that is the original form.

According to the Kufans, it is hal umma, the hamza being dropped by transferring its vowel to the lam, but this is far-fetched, because hal enters upon the imperative and is transitive, as in this verse, and intransitive, as in the words of God Most High: ﴿Come here to us﴾.

﴿Those who testify that God has forbidden this﴾: they are their leaders who support their statement. They were commanded to bring them forth so that the proof would be binding upon them, and by their inability to produce them their misguidance would be made manifest, and that they have no basis to hold on to, like one who follows them blindly. For this reason the witnesses are restricted by the genitive construction (idafa) and described with what indicates that they are witnesses well known for testifying in their favor and supporting their doctrine.

﴿And if they testify﴾ after they have come forth that God has forbidden this.

﴿Then do not testify with them﴾; that is, do not confirm them, for it is pure falsehood and sheer fabrication. Make clear to them its corruption, for accepting it from them would be agreement with them in false testimony.

﴿And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs﴾: the placing of the apparent noun in place of the pronoun is to indicate that whoever denies the signs of God Most High and sets up others alongside Him is a follower of desire and nothing else, and that whoever follows the proof cannot but confirm it.

﴿And those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, like the idol-worshippers, is conjoined to the first relative clause by way of conjoining an attribute to an attribute with the same subject, as in the verse of the poet:

"To the noble lord and the son of the Hima,
and the lion of the battalions in the crowd."

For whoever denies His signs, Exalted is He, does not believe in the Hereafter, and conversely.

﴿And they ascribe equals to their Lord﴾: that is, they make for Him equals. It is conjoined to "﴿do not believe﴾", and the meaning is: do not follow the desires of those who combine denial of God's signs, disbelief in the Hereafter, and associating others with Him, Glory be to Him. However, the prohibition does not revolve around that combination as such, but rather around the fact that those people possess all of these and are characterized by all of them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 151:

﴿Say: "Come."﴾ When the falsity of their claim became evident, namely that their associating partners with God, and their fathers doing so, and their forbidding what they forbade, were by the command and will of God Almighty, this became evident through their inability to produce anything they could rely on in that matter, and to bring forward witnesses who would testify to what they claimed regarding the prohibition, even after they had been challenged repeatedly and had clearly failed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to explain to them those forbidden things that the situation required him to explain, in the manner of wise discourse (al-usluub al-hakeem, the wise or skilful manner of address), as a notice that their duty was to avoid these forbidden things.

As for the forbidden foods, they were explained by God Almighty's words: ﴿Say: "I do not find ..."﴾ and so on, to the end of the verse. And "ta'aalaw" (come) is an imperative from "ta'aalin" (to rise high). Its original sense is that one who is in a high place says it to one who is below him, and then it was extended by generalisation, just as "ghaneemah" (booty) originally meant obtaining sheep from the enemy, and then it was used for obtaining anything taken from them, by extension, and then for gaining anything at all without hardship.

﴿Atlu﴾ (I will recite) is the answer to the imperative.

God Almighty's words ﴿what your Lord has forbidden﴾ are the object of this verb, with "ma" being a relative pronoun, and its returning pronoun omitted. The meaning is: "I will recite that which your Lord has forbidden," that is, the verses containing it. Or "ma" may be a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), meaning: "the verses containing its prohibition." Or the verb may be "harrama" (has forbidden), with "ma" taken as an interrogative, and the clause would then be the object of "atlu," because recitation is a kind of speech. It is as if it were said: "Say: What is it that your Lord has forbidden?"

﴿upon you﴾ is connected to "harrama" in every case. It has also been said that it is connected to "atlu." The first is more appropriate to the context of emphasis on obliging them to refrain from the forbidden things mentioned. This is also the reason for the mention of the title "Lord" together with the attachment to their pronoun, since reminding them that God is their Lord and absolute owner of their affairs is among the strongest motives for them to desist from what He has forbidden them, to the utmost degree of desistance.

The "an" (that) in God Almighty's words ﴿that you do not associate anything with Him﴾ explains the verb of recitation, which is linked to "what He has forbidden." The "la" (not) is prohibitive, as is indicated by the conjunction of what follows it with commands and prohibitions.

It is not necessary, for the coordinated element to explain the recitation of the forbidden things according to its literal wording, that the coordinated items also be of that kind, so that the commands could not be included in the conjunction with it. It is enough that they explain it in terms of its implications, which are the prohibitions concerning the opposites of what the commands concern. Commanding a thing necessarily implies prohibiting its opposite, and according to some scholars it is identical with it. It is as if the commands were mentioned and their implications were intended. The conjunction of the commands with the prohibitions that follow "an" (that), which explains the recitation of the forbidden things, together with the certainty that what is commanded is not forbidden, is clear evidence that the prohibition refers back to the opposites in the manner mentioned. It is as if it were said: "I will recite what your Lord has forbidden: that you do not associate anything with Him, and that you do not do evil to your parents." Except that it was put in the form of a command to do good to them, between the two prohibitions that surround it, in order to emphasise the obligation to observe their rights. Mere refraining from harming them is not sufficient to fulfil their rights. For this reason the prohibition of associating partners with God, which is the greatest of forbidden things and the gravest of major sins here and in all other places, is placed after it.

It has also been said that "an" is a governing particle (nasibah), and its place in the accusative is governed by "upon you," with the verb understood as an incitement (ighraa', urging a person to do something). It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an apposition (badaliyyah) to "what He has forbidden." It has been said that its returning pronoun is omitted and that "an la" is in the accusative, with "la" being superfluous. It has been said that it is in the genitive by implying the preposition "li" (for). It has been said that it is in the nominative, by supposing the implied recited statement to be "that you do not associate," or the forbidden thing to be "that you do not associate," with the addition of "la." It has been said that the position most relied upon is the first, for several reasons, among them that bringing the explained element into the form of a prohibition gives greater emphasis to the explanation of the prohibition.

God Almighty's words ﴿anything﴾ are in the accusative either as a verbal noun (masdariyyah, i.e. "in any way") or as an object (maf'uliyyah). The meaning is: "Do not associate anything with Him of association," or "anything among things."

﴿And to parents﴾: that is, "and do good to them both."

﴿Good treatment﴾, whose precise meaning has already been discussed.

﴿And do not kill your children﴾ is an obligation concerning the rights of children, which is placed after the obligation concerning the rights of parents. That is: do not kill them by burying them alive.

﴿For fear of poverty﴾: that is, because of poverty, as in God Almighty's words ﴿for fear of poverty﴾. It has been said that this refers to actual, present poverty, and that refers to anticipated poverty.

God Almighty's words ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾ form a new independent sentence, brought to give the reason for the prohibition, and to nullify the causal role of what they had taken as a cause for committing the forbidden act. It is also a guarantee from Him, Exalted is He, of their sustenance. That is: "We provide for both parties, not you. So do not fear poverty on the basis of your inability to obtain provision."

God Almighty's words ﴿And do not draw near to the indecencies﴾ are like His words ﴿And do not draw near to fornication, for it is an indecency ...﴾ to the end of the verse. However, the plural form is used here, intending to prohibit all their kinds.

For this reason, His words ﴿what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ are substituted for it. That is: what is done of them openly in shops, as is the custom of their base people, and what is done secretly by taking secret lovers, as is the habit of their nobles.

The linking of the prohibition to approaching them is either for the sake of emphasising deterrence from them, because the incentives towards them are strong, or because approaching them leads to committing them. The placing of the prohibition of them between the prohibition of killing children and the prohibition of killing in general, as occurs in the surah of the Children of Israel, is because, although it is in itself a great offence, it is in the same category as killing children, since the children of fornication are in the position of the dead.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning coitus interruptus (al-'azl): "That is a hidden burying alive (wa'd khafiyy)." From this it becomes clear that interpreting the indecencies as major sins in general, and interpreting ﴿what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ in the way that the apparent and hidden sin was interpreted earlier, is a kind of separating the bark from the tree.

﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden﴾: that is, which God has forbidden to be killed by granting it protection through Islam or through a covenant. Thus the combatant (harbi) is excluded from it.

God Almighty's words ﴿except by right﴾ are an exceptive construction lacking its complement (istithnaa' mufarragh), in the most general of states. That is: "Do not kill it in any state, except in the state of being attached to the right, which is the command of the Law to kill it." This occurs through disbelief after belief, fornication after marriage, and killing a soul that is protected. Or it is in the most general of causes: "Do not kill it by any cause except a cause of right, which is what has been mentioned." Or it is in the most general of verbal nouns: "Do not kill it with any killing except a killing that is by right, which is killing by one of the matters mentioned."

﴿That﴾ refers to the five obligations mentioned, and the sense of distance in it indicates the elevated rank of these among the legal obligations. It is the subject (mubtada').

God Almighty's words ﴿He has enjoined you with it﴾: that is, your Lord has commanded you with it, as an emphatic command, whose predicate is this. The sentence is a new independent sentence, brought to renew the covenant and to emphasise the obligation of observing what they were charged with.

Since the matters forbidden are of the kind that the immediate judgement of sound minds declares to be ugly, the noble verse is concluded with His words ﴿so that you may reason﴾: that is, so that you may use your intellects, which restrain your souls and hold them back from committing the ugly acts mentioned.

The reason the prohibition is directed at approaching his property is the emphasis already given in the prohibition against eating it. (And to exclude the beneficial approach from the ruling of the prohibition by way of exception:) that is, do not come near it in any manner whatsoever.

﴿Except in the way that is best﴾: except by the course that is best, that is, the best form of safeguarding, growing (the wealth), and the like.

The address is to the guardians and executors, because of His saying, ﴿until he reaches his maturity (ashudd)﴾. The phrase "until" marks the limit of what is understood from the exception, not of the prohibition itself. It is as if it were said: "Safeguard it until he becomes mature and sound in judgment, and then hand it over to him," as in His saying, ﴿If you perceive in them sound judgment, then deliver their property to them﴾.

Ashudd is the plural of shidda (strength), like ni'ma and an'um (blessing and blessings). Or it is the plural of shadd, like kalb and aklub (dog and dogs). Or it is the plural of shidd, like sirr and asir (a bond). It has also been said that it is a singular noun, like ankun (a form of the word for the strength of the youth).

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾: that is, with fairness and equity.

﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾: except what it can bear and what is not difficult for it. This is a parenthetical statement placed directly after the command to be just, to signal that observing justice is, just as it is, difficult. It is as if it were said: "Upon you is what is within your capacity, and whatever lies beyond it is pardoned for you."

﴿And when you speak﴾: a statement made in a judgment, a testimony, or something similar.

﴿Then be just﴾ in it. ﴿Even if it be a near relative﴾: that is, the one to whom it is said or against whom it is said.

﴿A near relative﴾: that is, a relative of yours. Do not incline toward them at all. The meaning of "even if" (law) in such a context has been clarified many times before.

﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾: that is, what He has enjoined upon you of the enumerated matters, or any covenant whatsoever, so that what has been mentioned enters into it first and foremost. Or it means the oaths and vows you have made with Allah. Its placement first is for the sake of giving attention to its importance.

﴿That﴾ refers to the obligations that have been detailed. The sense of distance (in "that") refers to what was mentioned earlier.

﴿He has enjoined you with it﴾: He commanded you with it as an emphatic command.

﴿That you may remember﴾: that you may remember what is contained within it and act according to its requirements. It is also read with the letter dhal shaddah (tadhakkarun, "that you may remember"). These are ten rulings that do not vary with the differences among nations or eras.

From Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father): "These are clear-cut verses (muhkamat) that nothing from among all the Books has abrogated. They are prohibitions upon all of the children of Adam. They are the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab). Whoever acts upon them enters Paradise, and whoever abandons them enters the Fire."

From Ka'b al-Ahbar: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ka'b, these verses are indeed the first thing in the Torah: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you...﴾" to the end of the verses.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 6, verse 153:

﴿And that this is My path﴾ is a reference to what was mentioned in the two verses concerning the commands and prohibitions; this is what Muqatil said. It was also said: it refers to what was mentioned in the surah as a whole, for all of it is about establishing monotheism (tawhid) and prophethood and explaining the Sharia (divine law).

It has been read as ﴿صِراطِي﴾ with a fatha on the ya'. The meaning of its being attributed to his pronoun (ﷺ) is that it is ascribed to him (ﷺ) in terms of the walking of the path, not in terms of its origination, as in ﴿صِراطُ اللَّهِ﴾ (the path of Allah).

The purpose is to show that the commands and prohibitions detailed are not restricted to those to whom it is recited, but are also related to him (ﷺ), and that he (ﷺ) is constant in acting upon them and observing them.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ (straight), are a confirmatory circumstantial state (hal mu'akkida), and the position of "anna" (that) together with what follows it is in the accusative by the omission of the particle of cause; that is: "and because this is My path," i.e., My way, straight.

﴿فاتَّبِعُوهُ﴾ (so follow it) is like the words of the Exalted: ﴿وَأنَّ المَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أحَدًا﴾ (And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone alongside Allah). The reason given for following it is that it is his (ﷺ) path, not that it is the path of Allah the Exalted, even though in itself it is also so; this is because his (ﷺ) walking in it calls creation to follow, since by that it becomes clear to them that it is the path of Allah, mighty and majestic.

It has been read with a kasra on the hamza, as a new sentence (isti'naf). It has also been read: ﴿أنْ هَذا﴾ with a lightened "anna", with its noun, which is the pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), omitted. It has also been read: ﴿سِراطِي﴾ (with sin), ﴿هَذا صِراطِي﴾, ﴿وهَذا صِراطُ رَبِّكم﴾ (and this is the path of your Lord), and ﴿وهَذا صِراطُ رَبِّكَ﴾ (and this is the path of your Lord).

﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ﴾ (And do not follow the ways): the differing religions, or the paths of innovations and misguidance.
